attendance_method: Downloaded the official Arab Health '2024 Post show results' PDF (arabhealthonline.com branded) and extracted its text. The statistics block reads: '3,304 delegates', '3,627 exhibitors', '78 exhibiting countries', '57,543 live visitors', '131,332 professional visits'. This is exactly the inflated-headcount trap: the 57,543 live visitors (and the 131,332 visit-events) are exhibition footfall, and 3,627 exhibitors are sellers, none of whom submit science. The only figure that describes people attending the conference programme is the 3,304 delegates, so that is the headline and the visitor count goes to alt_figures. The 2025 edition is widely reported at 58,000-130,000 attendees, but I did not load a 2025 post-show page confirming it, so 2025 is not recorded.
ratio_rationale: Arab Health is a medical trade exhibition with CME conference tracks attached. The conference programme is invited faculty speaking to a paying delegate audience; there is no open call for abstracts anywhere in the event materials, and the row's counted evidence was 0 contributed abstracts. Judged 1%: this is a place where essentially no contributed science happens — not a judgement about the attendees being the wrong sort, but about the programme having no submission channel for them to use. That is well below EuroPCR 6%, which is at least a medical society's own scientific teaching course. REVISED from my first pass, which used 2% only because that was the old floor of the valid range; with the floor now at 0.5% I am stating the number I actually believe. Note the ratio is applied to the clean 3,304 delegate figure, the only people attending the conference programme; the 57,543 live visitors and 3,627 exhibitors are trade-show footfall and booth staff, exactly the categories the brief says to discount, and converting that headline would overstate the row roughly 17-fold.
programme_evidence: Post-show report frames the event as 'the Middle East's #1 medical trade show' with exhibitors and visitors as the primary metrics and 'conference programs that featured experts sharing' — invited faculty, not submitted work.
character_evidence: https://www.exhibitor-catalogue.com/media/downloads/4dd65056-2ddc-483c-8067-bb92ebb3e916.pdf — trade exhibition plus invited-expert CME conference programme; no call for abstracts anywhere on the event materials

attendance_method: Loaded the ESPID 2025 prospectus 'Benefits of Attending & Past Statistics' page, which carries a six-year series the society sells to sponsors: ESPID 2019 (Ljubljana) 2,331 participants; 2020 (Virtual) 3,152; 2021 (Virtual) 3,107; 2022 (Athens & Online) 3,395; 2023 (Lisbon & Online) 3,684; 2024 (Copenhagen & Online) 3,034. Every figure from 2020 on is explicitly hybrid or virtual, so TOTAL_INC_VIRTUAL — the 2019 Ljubljana figure of 2,331 is the last clean in-person number and is the better guide to how many people are physically in the room.
ratio_rationale: ESPID is the paediatric counterpart of ESCMID: an open abstract call, accepted-abstract authors eligible for ESPID Participation and Travel Awards (people come BECAUSE an abstract was accepted), and abstracts published for the meeting. Judged 40%, directly against ESCMID 40% — the adult infectious-disease congress of the same shape and the same contributed-programme backbone. REVISED: my first pass cut this to 30% because the 3,034 headline is virtual-inclusive (Copenhagen & Online). That discount was wrong under the brief's rule — an abstract presented online is still an abstract and an online presenter is still a presenter — so the figure goes back to the shape-based 40%. Nothing in this headcount is exhibitor booth staff, trade-show footfall or accompanying persons, which are the only discountable categories, so no discount applies at all. Honest uncertainty: the online cohort is large (the in-person-only 2019 Ljubljana figure was 2,331 against 3,034 hybrid in 2024), and if online registrants submit at a materially lower rate than they attend, the true figure could sit nearer 32%; 40% is the reading I find most likely on programme shape.
programme_evidence: Open abstract call with ESPID Participation and Travel Awards restricted to accepted-abstract authors, alongside invited lectures from named researchers — the contributed track drives attendance.
character_evidence: https://2025.espidmeeting.org/ — open call for abstracts; accepted-abstract authors eligible for ESPID Participation and Travel Awards
